scenes.title: What is it?
scenes.narration: Channel-length modulation occurs when the transistor's channel length decreases as drain-to-source voltage increases, preventing the device from acting like an ideal current source.

scenes.title: The Saturation Formula
scenes.narration: In saturation, we model this by multiplying the drain current by a factor that accounts for the channel-length modulation coefficient, lambda.

visual.formula_where: λ is the channel-length modulation coefficient

scenes.title: Circuit Modeling
scenes.narration: We represent this effect in small-signal models by adding an output resistance, r-O, between the drain and source, which limits the maximum voltage gain.
